Not long after H.R. 1 passed the House, Republicans themselves admitted they hadn't read the bill. They didn't realize it banned AI regulation for a decade, or that it increased the deficit by $5 Trillion, or that it gutted Medicaid for 16 million people. The problem is, most Americans still have no idea what is in this bill. So, in writing about it, I was fortunate to connect with activist and designer [Jonathan J Daybear](https://open.substack.com/users/86807940-jonathan-j-daybear?utm_source=mentions), who has graciously put into a visual display the carnage that H.R. 1 will cause if it becomes law. With that, let us _show you_ why, regardless of your politics, you should oppose H.R. 1 from becoming law. **Let 's Address This.**
**Let 's Address This is made possible by you, the thoughtful reader. Support us by subscribing below.**

| [](https://substack.com/redirect/1303b92b-85c6-4fe0-9fab-6b843c6bf60b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
## National Debt
Remember how Republicans pretend to care about the National Debt whenever a Democrat is in the White House? Now that Republicans control the House, the Senate, and the White House, they're adding up to $5 Trillion to the National Debt.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/655eb41f-8396-4a33-87b6-c020e0120192?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
## Healthcare Access
These next three visuals demonstrate how horrific an impact H.R. 1 will have on basic healthcare access for tens of millions of Americans. In addition to stripping healthcare from up to 16 million people, H.R. 1 will close hospitals in the most rural parts of our nation. Thus the cruel irony of this piece of legislation--it will hurt Republican voters more than any other demographic. MAGAs just voted against their own healthcare access, and they will suffer the most as a result. By working to block this bill, Democratic Senators and Democratic voters are ultimately helping Republican voters more than anyone else.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/311cc857-b11a-434b-b065-c8ea7964c7d2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/60852f80-699e-4165-bb79-ba0e3c4b2b22?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/e46d8bbe-80c4-48bc-b65d-4602e06d52ad?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
## A New Tax Scam
The Trump 2017 Tax Scam was one of the biggest transfers of wealth from working class to the wealthy. In fact, it built upon the now nearly half century long Reaganomics tricle down scam started in the 1980s. A recent study by Rand found that these tax cuts for the super wealthy have resulted in a transfer of [$79 TRILLION in wealth](https://substack.com/redirect/e0e89128-c761-4e7d-a324-38302260e037?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) from the bottom 90% to the top 1%.
**If you 're finding value in this analysis, support our efforts by subscribing.**
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack..4IWqgTkCY9O5spGm1cmz17H3ldPhdJgZSRANjcvV4RQ?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget-preamble&utm_content=167128952)
And now, H.R. 1 wants to give billionaires even more money, and make working people suffer even more than we already are. The below graphic shows who gets tax cuts, and who pays more. Those making over $4.3 million a year get a $389K tax cut, while those making under $51,000 a year get a tax hike. This is class warfare, and Republicans are working for billionaires.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/05d50ff9-f342-4781-ba09-446649450fea?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
## The United Police States of America
Next, H.R. 1 further transforms the United States into a police state--and that's not an understatement. These next four images show that picture. It is truly mortifying how, while cutting access to healthcare and food, MAGAs want to build a vanity wall that will nothing to actually address immigration, increase ICE funding to round up Americans, increase prisons to grow the private enslavement industry, and increase the already bloated military budget to continue to wage war. Like Tupac said, "They got money for war but can't feed the poor."
First, $8 billion for 10,000 new ICE fascist agents, with the plan to round up 3,000 Americans per day. A recent study by the CATO institute found that of the 204,000 people ICE has arrested and detained in just the last year, 65% had no criminal record, and 93% had no violent record. Trump claims he's targeting violent immigrants, but more than 93% of the people he is targeting have no violent record whatsoever. Adding $8 billion to his fascist initiative will further destroy our civil rights.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/04e2a25e-3641-4b25-8717-d70c9a9236db?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Rounding up 3,000 people a day will require concentrating them into camps--concentration camps, if you will. Therefore, H.R. 1 adds $59 billion to build more prisons for people caught by masked ICE fascists. This isn't freedom, it's fascism.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/805ed955-edaa-416d-a24b-58cdff4a3302?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
And of course, why invest in a humane immigration policy when we can just burn $50 billion on building a vanity wall that will solve absolutely nothing? A reminder that this is a white supremacist policy. There are conservatively more than 600,000 undocumented Canadian and European mostly white immigrants in America. When was the last time Trump proposed building a northern wall or having ICE raid white majority neighborhoods? Never.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/2ce274e1-249c-4469-b76f-e9f3c7bd7967?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Finally, in addition to becoming a domestic police state, Trump wants the United States to become the world police, even more so than it already is. Another $150 billion to an already bloated military budget is money that will go to defense contractors to build more weapons of war. Those weapons of war will be used to fund genocide in Palestine, bomb Yemen and Syria, and fund the global arms trade. None of this makes us safer. All of it makes the world a less peaceful place.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/ea8af72d-4fb2-4d94-8390-adca0864043b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
## Who Do We Call To Stop H.R. 1?
Below are the Republican Senators who have indicated the possibility of voting NO on H.R. 1. We only need 4 of them to flip and vote no on this absurd piece of legislation. Below, after this graphic is a sample script to use when you call them.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/5cac5a5e-b5f3-47f8-aeea-42a9689ed30a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
> **CALL SCRIPT:**
> **IF CALLING:**
> Hi, my name is [NAME], and I'm a voter from [CITY]. I'm calling with urgency to demand that [Senator NAME] vote **NO** on H.R. 1, the budget reconciliation bill.
> This bill is dangerous. It guts vital programs our families and communities rely on--programs that fund healthcare, education, food assistance, and our civil rights. Stripping these resources is not fiscal responsibility--it's cruelty.
> A vote for H.R. 1 is a vote against working families. Against children. Against seniors. Against your own constituents. And I promise you--we're paying attention, and we won't forget.
> Vote NO on H.R. 1. Protect your people. Thank you.
> **IF LEAVING A VOICEMAIL:**
> My name is [FULL NAME]. I'm a voter, and I'm urging Senator [NAME] to vote NO on H.R. 1. This bill harms working people. This is a critical vote--and I will remember it.
## Conclusion
H.R. 1 isn't just another bill--it's a blueprint for authoritarianism wrapped in corporate greed. It is an assault on working people, on civil rights, on our healthcare, our democracy, and our shared humanity. It punishes the vulnerable and rewards the wealthy. It rips food from hungry families while handing billionaires another tax break. It guts healthcare for 16 million Americans while funneling billions into ICE raids, private prisons, and endless war. It isn't policy--it's cruelty made law.
But as of this article, this fight isn't over. In fact, it can still be won.
We only need **four Republican Senators** to stand up for the people. Just four to stop this catastrophic legislation from becoming law. And we know public pressure works. Your voice matters. Your calls matter. Your courage matters.
So call. Share. Organize. Speak truth with clarity and conviction. And if you value this work--if you believe in the power of independent, people-driven advocacy to elevate the truth and defend our democracy--then I ask for your support. [Become a free or paid subscriber to ](https://substack.com/redirect/96ce2ce5-a244-4219-991f-65c6e1ee05a6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)_[Let's Address This](https://substack.com/redirect/96ce2ce5-a244-4219-991f-65c6e1ee05a6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)._ Help me continue to report, resist, and rally for a republic that works for all of us--not just the wealthy few.
We are not powerless. But if we stay silent, we are complicit. Let's fight back--loudly and together.
I am doing everything in my power over the next four years to stave off fascism in the United States, and I need your support.**Subscribe and join the movement.**

While Republicans are working to enrich themselves and their ultra-wealthy allies, their budget is focused on ripping Medicaid from millions of Americans, cutting SNAP benefits and letting people go hungry, and expanding Trump’s tax cuts for the wealthiest few.

| | Hi Friend, This weekend, I had the honor of marching alongside Lateefah Simon at **San Francisco Pride**. There was no better place to celebrate Pride and affirm our commitment to equal rights than in San Francisco – a city that has shaped LGBTQ+ history– and I couldn’t be more proud to march by Lateefah’s side. [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/110514160/554613824/784544418?&refcode=E13994-20250628-McBrideSplit-Image-SplitSend&amount=25&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTAvMS8xMDQ0NDUiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiN2M5MTk2NzQtNGU1NS1mMDExLThmN2MtNjA0NWJkZmU4ZTljIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=fnLVajUdYgL0-9bMqzsDiexdju-9hb0VawyTvR1eyoE=) Pride has always been about both joy and resistance. About celebrating who we are and standing up for each other in the face of hate, fear, and injustice. **That’s why I’m so proud to stand with Lateefah.** She is a tireless fighter—someone who leads with heart, courage, and an unwavering commitment to inclusion and equity. She’s spent her life advancing civil rights, expanding opportunity, and delivering for communities that too often go unheard. Her voice is exactly what we need in Congress. subject: I’m up the creek without a paddle
body:
I'm in a bind, and I need your help, Peter.

I’m up the creek without a paddle, Peter.
The battle for America’s future is heating up, and the Democrats are pouring all their resources into taking back the House and Senate. They're still reeling from President Trump's historic comeback, and they'll stop at nothing to undermine his agenda and our Republican Majority.
**_As a conservative defending Montana's Second Congressional District seat, I'm on the frontlines of this battle. _**
I'm Troy Downing, an Air Force veteran with a proven track record of putting it all on the line for our country. I flew helicopters into war zones, built successful small businesses from scratch, and I'm not about to back down from the Radical Left now. [](https://trk.emails.troydowning.) But I need your help, Peter. The Q2 FEC deadline is looming, and our fundraising numbers are lagging WAY behind. If we don't turn things around quickly, we risk losing our House Majority and giving the Democrats the opening they need to sabotage President Trump's agenda.
**I'm not sugarcoating it** – the stakes are high, and the consequences of failure are dire. **__I'm counting on 5,000 Patriots like you to chip in $25 or $30 before the Q2 FEC deadline. __**
Your support is the only way we can protect our Majority and keep pushing forward with President Trump's America-first agenda.
[Can you find it in your heart to step forward and help a humble veteran like me today?](https://trk.emails.troydowning.) [ SUPPORT TROY DOWNING

Troy Downing Air Force Veteran, 129th Rescue Squadron |

## Big Beautiful Bill Clears Key Senate Test
President Trump’s [Big Beautiful Bill cleared a major hurdle](http://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0LGO8yAQBOCnwV0sWLBJCoq_cZe_vdJaYIn3hE1ko6Dk6U--V7hupJE-aebrPt-RM2-P_7iSq6nMG7UjU620z6EcKwePB3nMGRkfWBcMyz6DhOEix4uWc0TO79l00SUiIN2RU3ZQYK01ultcUjiopNFeb1rFmzfgzaiGW7LRXkOAjt2pyVFLJSWA6tMYopQBVFL6SuCFkRS5lr3_LrzVhVJ-lxftfShrl91S6_MQ-p-AScDUWuu9D2cnYDrHCJhwrxwynTGooW3afOTHlG538dk4Zz5GK4x8rMj5V61_uuLl4CcAAP__2C1xMQ) late Saturday, advancing to full Senate debate after a razor-thin 51–49 vote. The [breakthrough came after hours of negotiations](http://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLHOnDAQhJ8GOp_sNQc0LtLQ_WlTorW9xhsZjPDe_bm3j8grpJ5Po5nv19f6hVz42H7iTk5SXQ_6boVE6FpDbTsHj408loKMG0rGkK8VNDyVHpXVa0Qun3Xoo0tEQLYnZ6angWmaBttnhx7tgDr4SDBiSADDPOMwj8nOdrLYs7vb9Gi10RrAPNIYotYBTDJ2JvDdoCmy1Ovxu_IhmVL51Dddj1D3vrgscrbO_uhg6WCRTJlLubMOllx3ug91sGDc-eAmFwrX4yav134qyaQO-iPKaK0ifm70aadhNEYVfpN6nRGFmmp0oJDa6qk8b8oTvoTTqyjPpXSw9JeL5zeXwm2cukFvO_K_Gb38l9e3g78BAAD__wiZjUc) with Republican holdouts, capped by a late-night huddle between Vice President JD Vance and Senate Majority Leader John Thune (R-S.D.), who secured support by promising deeper Medicaid cuts. Senators Rand Paul (R-Ky.) and Thom Tillis (R-N.C.) voted no—Paul over debt ceiling concerns, and Tillis in protest of projected Medicaid shortfalls for North Carolina. Shortly after the vote, [Tillis announced he won’t seek re-election in 2026](http://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkL2upDAMhZ8mdB4FwwBTUGxDd7fdEjnEgHdDghLPXM3br5hXuJ3lI33n58_X_EUSJG6_6eBR1zRH_i6BVTnPSyqHLI4KOwqBhDbSnZY9z2jxDraDxs6eJLzntvLjyozcVDzW_b3Gvu_bptpHT8wtU-PcfRhc27rF--FBzI8FHwM2lYwXzXaNra1FrG9rt3hrF6zXuhkYnWkte9GUb3-TRN15De_04nxb0lGFcVc9i2l-GZwMTvF9pqKXZHC6wAYn2133w-D0LHD1Mzht6YTCEXRPB6iEIAVOKoULpAiZOfCikiI48UCrcoai6Z_EDTQ_j7OAZAb3hlfS60kbSSwKTjZwTE-V9RnASQgGpyqP_vz-mHS9ae12kIRPfP3R5q8R_wcAAP__WA6YGQ), citing a “breakdown in Republican priorities.” Democrats stalled the bill’s momentum by forcing clerks to read all 940 pages aloud—a marathon that [lasted nearly 16 hours and wrapped up Sunday afternoon](http://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLFuwyAURb8GNkfwsKEeGLp4S9eO1gOezauwiWyUKH9fpfmErvdeHeme7-t8RS68r1-4kW9LnXd6nIVao2OO9dw4BjwpYCnIuGLLGPMxg4KhU7Yzak7I5Tn3MvmFCMhI8toNGpxzvZHZj2kxaMH1agwhWSQVh6A1BNtrQNCS_YumrFFaKQB9WWxMSkXQizYfBEH0ihK3elx-Ku8t01Ke9U7HJdZNFp9bu53CfAqYBEwtU-ZSXp2AKdeNXocETCft2EjANBg3jG7s3kEXuJTuIEy8r12i8B7Jw6fbg0vh0zrRq3VD_oPK9i9Ldw-_AQAA__9PZXqT). The Senate now enters 20 hours of debate, followed by a flood of amendment votes in what’s known as a “vote-a-rama.” Final passage is expected sometime today.
## Sniper Opens Fire on Idaho Firefighters
Two people were killed Sunday after a [sniper ambushed firefighters responding to a blaze](http://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkL2OpDAQhJ8GMkbtH2gIHFwy2Vx6IWrsBvfJ4JHxzmjefsW-woalkqr0ff8e84MkybH9pZ1dXfN88PtMXCuX2edzF7_QyQulREIb1Ug-llmD7jsYOgNzIEmf2bbBrcyaTctOYa80IlrTRjetsCgMPS7WjBZxBB96GoxHRFwn1Yq71mAwoAC0Vrd18AHAa7UqM7JeGgscpOZy-5_lqJHX9MkvLjef9za5WOvzbMyfRt8bfafnBXBVVyhVfOJG333mr9IFSnxwJ4Fi7s6Yc5Vj63pkq6wZrPY9AU9jUMZCrwiVRRqntrjwfEtKcg7YWNh2kvRzXn9l7OX0dwAAAP__GPd8hA) on Canfield Mountain near Coeur d’Alene, Idaho. Authorities said the shooter, who remained at large Sunday night, unleashed gunfire for hours, forcing crews to retreat and halting firefighting efforts. Sheriff Bob Norris confirmed multiple firefighters were targeted. Officials are still unsure if there are additional casualties or how many suspects may be involved. Gov. The Texas Water Development Board (TWDB) directed water planners for Dallas-Fort Worth and Northeast Texas to [resolve a dispute](http://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJyskLGOszAQhJ_GdKD12sZQuIh-iS5_eyUyeEmsGByZVUje_pTo7g2uHI30jb75Oo9nH1PcLv_9So6fSx43OvZEzFTGQjuVR45lztuS4swTvfI2i39KnPp9REBTQ1srGIOP6TXqKrgJQi8rctIaiZ1Usq-uzoBC6oKaTL9Y7EFbY-0Ck4Zg0He2iu4Ng1aBlCBN2_gOSQcZ0PdeI7VCA4XIuTR8Jaan35f0yg8qzZzXKrkr830X6iRwEDgcx9HciG_vUuDwVhI4pDz7VP-ED6M-PFOpp-xLqFcijtul_pUVOFTFhfsRU4p7a4WGy-pj-izyH5z1cPgdAAD__0unfxg) over the proposed 66,000-acre Marvin Nichols Reservoir, officially declaring an interregional conflict for the third time since 2011.

---|---
**Good Morning!** On this day in 1875, the _Frontier Echo_ [published its first edition](http://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJys0DGuqzAQheHVmA7kGWMSFy6iJ9HltbdEAx6CJceObCuE3V-RNdzqr85XnJ_7dCcffHz8pyfb-lnTFHkvgWvlPGUunN_J5yXFNfilznykuIh_StxMmVCibuXQKjk58uGY-sbZWToDDVu4aMArKDDNZuE60AJIEiWvgAbkRc-kjOJ-1Q5N4-2JyUFJAAl66OiK3DtwSIZ65EH0kp2vKXd148ofKms40ptzt6RnE-xW66sIdRM4Chz3fe9q2SjF4CN3KT8Ejt9V6-ho5-OMwJFjzWe1hiZb99p9CL4MF9HLx5N8-OL1D355W_wNAAD__y3PdzA) in Jacksboro. The newspaper, which focused on the cattle industry in West Texas, eventually became the _Albany News_, which remains in publication today. ## Conflict Over Marvin Nichols Reservoir Heats Up
The Texas Water Development Board (TWDB) directed water planners for Dallas-Fort Worth and Northeast Texas to [resolve a dispute](http://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJyskL2O3SAUhJ8Gd1j8GdsFxSrS7TZtSusYDusTYVgBsfe-fXRXyhuknxnN9_16396BEuWPn3Ci61-xbBnvlrB3rFvFhvUqVH3JMZHvOz5L9uyHZm9r25RQExeWa7EFoPTczBDcLsIqB3RynqRapJbrcDg_L0tcrJzNukxqN977uOsY4yrBI0wDudeYsFpIKeRkR1gUmiCDghWMQsuMwEC91LEf2PELWkzPcmEdfTmH5I7ePxvTb0w9mHrc9z2-OPjv8qdmSK8QU4_vHr-hY-V7gRp4qQFr4ycGgk4lc8r8hHpR5pn8UVLj_9iZekDt5BNuCizCbCUHrVY-iTnwxRjkXkxG74gaPIxHP9NQXfi8KSVqdmZGfJxA32eG_h9kX079DQAA__-UA5Xk) over the proposed 66,000-acre Marvin Nichols Reservoir, officially declaring an interregional conflict for the third time since 2011. Last week, Zohran Mamdani posted a resounding victory in New York City's Democratic primary. It was a shocking outcome to many, as Zohran was young and unknown taking on Andrew Cuomo, who had money, the establishment and universal name ID, albeit with very mixed feelings among many voters from his time as Governor.
I think Zohran is likely to have a walkover in November unless the current field of Eric Adams, Jim Walden, Curtis Sliwa and Andrew Cuomo consolidates to just one or two candidates, and even then you'd have to project Zohran as the heavy favorite. He is very likely the city's next mayor.
Zohran triumphed despite the NYTimes and others clearly having it out for him. The institutions have less sway than ever, and voters are hungry for something new.
The reactions have been all over the map. People have been calling me with questions ranging from excitement to "Should I leave the city?"
I met with Zohran and Cuomo, as well as multiple other mayoral candidates before the primary. They met with me to seek advice but also an endorsement, as they thought I could move some voters their way. I declined to endorse for a number of reasons. I had former staffers and colleagues associated with 4 different campaigns, and didn't want to step on anyone out of loyalty to another. I see my role as an Independent reformer of the system. Last, I had complicated feelings and thoughts.
I had met Zohran prior to this campaign and sat down with him a number of weeks ago. I found him to be a good person who wants good things for people. He's a sincere and talented messenger. He is positive and not the least bit hateful or corrupt. He is newly married and comes across as dedicated and energetic.
I also think Zohran is smart and adaptable. Some folks who are ideological come across as stuck in their thinking - I don't think that's an issue with Zohran. I believe he will figure out a lot of things in real time. He certainly figured out a lot about how to connect with people as a candidate.
Big picture, I agree with his goal of making New York City more affordable. The rent in New York has gotten higher and higher - I hear it from young people I work with all of the time and can scarcely believe what they're paying. One person I know who is working in hospitality is paying close to $4,000 for an apartment that would have cost me $1,500 25 years ago. I like the idea of free child care - it is indeed very difficult and expensive to manage it on your own. Trying to make New York more affordable for the vast majority of its residents is a worthy vision.
Having a young, smart, dynamic mayor with good intentions who will show up for events and neighborhoods big or small and put his best foot forward is a major upgrade among several dimensions. That's a pretty good summary of why he won. Who would choose the scandal-tarred 67-year old over the next generation?
But I have some concerns, some of which are within Zohran's control, some of which aren't.
First, it's unclear how much of Zohran's economic agenda he'll be able to implement and how it would work. Raising taxes on the wealthy for example requires the state legislature to approve, and Governor Hochul has already said that would be a non-starter for her. Would she change her tune next year after Zohran is sworn in? I'm dubious. Free buses sound great, but homeless or near-homeless people would be more likely to use the buses when they're free and air-conditioned, and you could see the quality of experience go down. Even working-class New Yorkers might miss paying for the bus, which is definitely the cheapest way to get around. City-run grocery stores are a bad idea and would compete with mom-and-pop shops; if you're not trying to fill food deserts you're much better off simply giving people vouchers for groceries at existing stores that have razor-thin margins to begin with.
I love the idea of a mayor who wants to make the city work better for working families. That's a win. I studied this when I ran for mayor, and the mayor's ability to actually make things more affordable is somewhat limited in scope. I think a lot of people, including Zohran himself, are going to be frustrated at how little the average New Yorker's cost structure will change.
Meanwhile, business people are very nervous with a self-described socialist heading to City Hall. Imagining that all of these CEO-types will stick around New York under all circumstances is incorrect. You can't think that people who run businesses are profiteering assholes on one hand, but then also that they're not up to making a ruthless decision based on different tax rates or relationship with government on the other. If I were Zohran, I'd get in front of as many major business leaders as possible and say, look, you may not always get what you want but you'll have a line to my administration, if only to complain. A lot of them want the city's help clearing red tape and whatnot. Giving them face time would get some of them to give you a chance before relocating to Florida.
They're nervous too because Zohran is 33 years old without a ton of managerial experience. A lot of it will be based on who he gets to run the agencies. Zohran for example should ask Police Commissioner Jessica Tisch to stay on. That would inspire a ton of confidence and continuity. Maria Torres-Springer is another administrator with a great reputation for competence. Build a team that signals professionalism and pragmatism as quickly as possible and it would soothe some nerves.
Zohran has said that law enforcement needs help. He has taken the progressive approach of saying we need more mental health professionals and resources, which sounds good. But among police officers themselves, morale is low and more officers are taking early retirement or moving to find work in Long Island or the suburbs. In my view, you need more officers and should go into recruitment mode. I was endorsed by the police captains' union and believed that the police force was key to the city's success. I think culturally that will be a stretch for Zohran.
Zohran has also pledged more resources to combat hate crimes. According to police data, 345 hate crimes were committed against Jews in New York last year, almost one per day. That's compared to 78 based on sexual orientation and 43 against Muslims in the same period.
I was troubled by Zohran's academic defense of the phrase "Globalize the Intifada" because it's a term used by some to justify violence against Jews. My Jewish friends in New York fear that they're more likely to be attacked on the street now than they were a couple years ago, and that this will get much worse under a Mamdani administration.
Unfortunately, I think they're right. Antisemitism is real. There are hateful people who will feel emboldened by Zohran's victory and will use it as an excuse to take out their anger and bigotry on another New Yorker.
This speaks to the fundamental fear I have for Zohran. I believe he is in public service to do good and improve people's lives, which itself might be unusual in this day and age. But in practice the job may become more about trying to keep very bad things from happening in a big, fractious city.
For example, if I had won the mayor's race in 2021, I would have faced some very tough situations. I would have had to curtail services to migrants, saying "Look, we are a good and welcoming city, but we also have limited resources. We cannot expend them on the world's migrants who have come to this country." I would have been attacked as being anti-black and anti-brown. Someone would have beaten up some Asians on the street, because they didn't have a security detail. There are constant trade-offs and no right answer. You just make a call knowing that you might look like shit.
Let's stipulate that Zohran is a good person. This is an era that manipulates us and turns politics into a clash of personalities. Doing what you think is the right thing could feed into the polarization and lead to chaos.
Let's imagine a scenario; ICE raids pick up under Trump in New York City. Videos of cruelty and masked goons grabbing Latinos and Muslims surface. Mayor Mamdani says, "We are a sanctuary city, we do not give our neighbors up!" President Trump relishes a clash and sends in the National Guard to back up ICE, something as happened in Los Angeles but on a bigger scale. The young Mayor refuses to let go of a detainee and is arrested. He is held for days. His followers erupt in protest. Jumaane Williams takes over as acting mayor. While Zohran is held, violence breaks out. Someone's house is burned down. Trump uses the disorder to send in more troops.
During this time, images of riots fill the screens. The police are reluctant to put themselves in harm's way. Attacks on Jews spike. Mayor Mamdani, finally free of ICE, gives an address, saying that "We are better than this. New York is a city of peace and goodwill." But a sense of disorder fills the air. A major firm decides to leave New York as well as hundreds of families. Conditions deteriorate and passions rise.
Being mayor of New York has not been kind to the futures of Eric Adams, Bill DeBlasio, Mike Bloomberg, or Rudy Giuliani. It's the kind of job that eats people up.
One reason some held their nose and voted for Andrew Cuomo was the sense that New York City is a diverse land of 8.2 million packed into a compressed area and a bit of a powderkeg. New York City Democrats, including a ton of new voters, chose a young, idealistic leader. I like Zohran. I hope it works out, for him and the city. But I think Zohran is going to have to adopt some new attributes very quickly - what got him here may not be what he now needs to succeed. It may sound crazy, but winning the primary might have been the easy part compared with what's to come.

clean_body: Last week, Zohran Mamdani posted a resounding victory in New York City's Democratic primary. | | ---|---|--- | | | Forwarded this email? ? for more | | ---|---|--- * | | | Jun 30 | | | | | | | | | | | | | | ---|---|--- Last week, Zohran Mamdani posted a resounding victory in New York City's Democratic primary. It was a shocking outcome to many, as Zohran was young and unknown taking on Andrew Cuomo, who had money, the establishment and universal name ID, albeit with very mixed feelings among many voters from his time as Governor. I think Zohran is likely to have a walkover in November unless the current field of Eric Adams, Jim Walden, Curtis Sliwa and Andrew Cuomo consolidates to just one or two candidates, and even then you'd have to project Zohran as the heavy favorite. He is very likely the city's next mayor. Zohran triumphed despite the NYTimes and others clearly having it out for him. The institutions have less sway than ever, and voters are hungry for something new. The reactions have been all over the map. People have been calling me with questions ranging from excitement to "Should I leave the city?" I met with Zohran and Cuomo, as well as multiple other mayoral candidates before the primary. They met with me to seek advice but also an endorsement, as they thought I could move some voters their way. I declined to endorse for a number of reasons. I had former staffers and colleagues associated with 4 different campaigns, and didn't want to step on anyone out of loyalty to another. I see my role as an Independent reformer of the system. Last, I had complicated feelings and thoughts. I had met Zohran prior to this campaign and sat down with him a number of weeks ago. I found him to be a good person who wants good things for people. He's a sincere and talented messenger. He is positive and not the least bit hateful or corrupt. He is newly married and comes across as dedicated and energetic. I also think Zohran is smart and adaptable. Some folks who are ideological come across as stuck in their thinking - I don't think that's an issue with Zohran. I believe he will figure out a lot of things in real time. He certainly figured out a lot about how to connect with people as a candidate. Big picture, I agree with his goal of making New York City more affordable. The rent in New York has gotten higher and higher - I hear it from young people I work with all of the time and can scarcely believe what they're paying. One person I know who is working in hospitality is paying close to $4,000 for an apartment that would have cost me $1,500 25 years ago. I like the idea of free child care - it is indeed very difficult and expensive to manage it on your own. Trying to make New York more affordable for the vast majority of its residents is a worthy vision. Having a young, smart, dynamic mayor with good intentions who will show up for events and neighborhoods big or small and put his best foot forward is a major upgrade among several dimensions. That's a pretty good summary of why he won. Who would choose the scandal-tarred 67-year old over the next generation? But I have some concerns, some of which are within Zohran's control, some of which aren't. First, it's unclear how much of Zohran's economic agenda he'll be able to implement and how it would work. Raising taxes on the wealthy for example requires the state legislature to approve, and Governor Hochul has already said that would be a non-starter for her. Would she change her tune next year after Zohran is sworn in? I'm dubious. Free buses sound great, but homeless or near-homeless people would be more likely to use the buses when they're free and air-conditioned, and you could see the quality of experience go down. Even working-class New Yorkers might miss paying for the bus, which is definitely the cheapest way to get around. City-run grocery stores are a bad idea and would compete with mom-and-pop shops; if you're not trying to fill food deserts you're much better off simply giving people vouchers for groceries at existing stores that have razor-thin margins to begin with. I love the idea of a mayor who wants to make the city work better for working families. That's a win. I studied this when I ran for mayor, and the mayor's ability to actually make things more affordable is somewhat limited in scope. I think a lot of people, including Zohran himself, are going to be frustrated at how little the average New Yorker's cost structure will change. Meanwhile, business people are very nervous with a self-described socialist heading to City Hall. Imagining that all of these CEO-types will stick around New York under all circumstances is incorrect. You can't think that people who run businesses are profiteering assholes on one hand, but then also that they're not up to making a ruthless decision based on different tax rates or relationship with government on the other. If I were Zohran, I'd get in front of as many major business leaders as possible and say, look, you may not always get what you want but you'll have a line to my administration, if only to complain. A lot of them want the city's help clearing red tape and whatnot. Giving them face time would get some of them to give you a chance before relocating to Florida. They're nervous too because Zohran is 33 years old without a ton of managerial experience. A lot of it will be based on who he gets to run the agencies. Zohran for example should ask Police Commissioner Jessica Tisch to stay on. That would inspire a ton of confidence and continuity. Maria Torres-Springer is another administrator with a great reputation for competence. Build a team that signals professionalism and pragmatism as quickly as possible and it would soothe some nerves. Zohran has said that law enforcement needs help. He has taken the progressive approach of saying we need more mental health professionals and resources, which sounds good. But among police officers themselves, morale is low and more officers are taking early retirement or moving to find work in Long Island or the suburbs. In my view, you need more officers and should go into recruitment mode. I was endorsed by the police captains' union and believed that the police force was key to the city's success. I think culturally that will be a stretch for Zohran. Zohran has also pledged more resources to combat hate crimes. According to police data, 345 hate crimes were committed against Jews in New York last year, almost one per day. That's compared to 78 based on sexual orientation and 43 against Muslims in the same period. I was troubled by Zohran's academic defense of the phrase "Globalize the Intifada" because it's a term used by some to justify violence against Jews. My Jewish friends in New York fear that they're more likely to be attacked on the street now than they were a couple years ago, and that this will get much worse under a Mamdani administration. Unfortunately, I think they're right. Antisemitism is real. There are hateful people who will feel emboldened by Zohran's victory and will use it as an excuse to take out their anger and bigotry on another New Yorker. This speaks to the fundamental fear I have for Zohran. I believe he is in public service to do good and improve people's lives, which itself might be unusual in this day and age. But in practice the job may become more about trying to keep very bad things from happening in a big, fractious city. For example, if I had won the mayor's race in 2021, I would have faced some very tough situations. I would have had to curtail services to migrants, saying "Look, we are a good and welcoming city, but we also have limited resources. We cannot expend them on the world's migrants who have come to this country." I would have been attacked as being anti-black and anti-brown. Someone would have beaten up some Asians on the street, because they didn't have a security detail. There are constant trade-offs and no right answer. You just make a call knowing that you might look like shit. Let's stipulate that Zohran is a good person. This is an era that manipulates us and turns politics into a clash of personalities. Doing what you think is the right thing could feed into the polarization and lead to chaos. Let's imagine a scenario; ICE raids pick up under Trump in New York City. Videos of cruelty and masked goons grabbing Latinos and Muslims surface. Mayor Mamdani says, "We are a sanctuary city, we do not give our neighbors up!" President Trump relishes a clash and sends in the National Guard to back up ICE, something as happened in Los Angeles but on a bigger scale. The young Mayor refuses to let go of a detainee and is arrested. He is held for days. His followers erupt in protest. Jumaane Williams takes over as acting mayor. While Zohran is held, violence breaks out. Someone's house is burned down. Trump uses the disorder to send in more troops. During this time, images of riots fill the screens. The police are reluctant to put themselves in harm's way. Attacks on Jews spike. Mayor Mamdani, finally free of ICE, gives an address, saying that "We are better than this. New York is a city of peace and goodwill." But a sense of disorder fills the air. A major firm decides to leave New York as well as hundreds of families. Conditions deteriorate and passions rise. Being mayor of New York has not been kind to the futures of Eric Adams, Bill DeBlasio, Mike Bloomberg, or Rudy Giuliani. It's the kind of job that eats people up. One reason some held their nose and voted for Andrew Cuomo was the sense that New York City is a diverse land of 8.2 million packed into a compressed area and a bit of a powderkeg. New York City Democrats, including a ton of new voters, chose a young, idealistic leader. I like Zohran. I hope it works out, for him and the city. But I think Zohran is going to have to adopt some new attributes very quickly - what got him here may not be what he now needs to succeed. It may sound crazy, but winning the primary might have been the easy part compared with what's to come. To see what Forward is doing for political choice in your area, . Republicans aren’t just threatening LGTBQIA+ people with harmful rhetoric — they’re turning it into law. Since Trump took office again this year, here’s what they’ve done:

• They **banned** gender-affirming care for trans kids (including adults) in over 20 states.

• They **erased** federal recognition of transgender people.

• They **banned** trans girls from school sports nationwide.

• They’re trying to **remove** Pride flags in schools, libraries, and government buildings.

• They’re pushing laws **forcing** trans people to use the wrong bathrooms.

• They’re **cutting** LGBTQIA+ suicide prevention funding from the 988 crisis line.

• They’re **gutting** DEI programs and blocking LGBTQ+ history in schools.

• They’re allowing red states like Iowa to **strip** civil rights protections for trans people entirely.

This isn’t just a rollback of rights — it’s a full-blown assault on our humanity.

[The Voter Protection Project is fighting back by working to defeat Republican anti-LGTBQIA+ extremists by replacing them with Democrats who will protect LGTBQIA+ people — and the democracy we depend on. They know they can’t win fairly, so they’re rigging the system to strip us of our rights — one bill, one vote, one voice at a time.

The Build Up Mississippi Act (House Bill 1), signed into law by Governor Tate Reeves on March 27, 2025, is a transformative piece of legislation aimed at phasing out Mississippi's state personal income tax, reducing the state grocery sales tax, increasing the gasoline tax, and granting local governments the authority to adjust grocery taxes under specific conditions. The Act seeks to eliminate the state's 4.4% flat personal income tax over the next decade, positioning Mississippi as the first state with an existing income tax to legislate its complete removal. Below is a detailed explanation of the Act, including its tax cuts, tax increases, and provisions for local government grocery tax adjustments.
**Overview of the Build Up Mississippi Act**
The Act outlines a gradual elimination of the personal income tax through annual reductions and revenue-based triggers, with full elimination targeted for the mid-2030s, contingent on economic growth. To offset revenue losses and stimulate the economy, the legislation reduces the state's grocery sales tax, increases the gasoline tax, and allows local governments to impose or increase grocery taxes. The goal is to enhance Mississippi's economic competitiveness, attract businesses and workers, and align the state with no-income-tax states like Texas, Florida, and Tennessee.
**Tax Cuts in the Build Up Mississippi Act**
1. Personal Income Tax Reduction and Phase-Out:
* Initial Cuts: Beginning in 2027, the state's flat 4.4% personal income tax rate will decrease by 0.25% annually, reaching 3% by 2030.
* Trigger-Based Reductions: Post-2030, further cuts will be tied to "growth triggers," where reductions occur only if state revenue exceeds spending projections. Sustained economic growth could eliminate the income tax entirely by the mid-2030s.
* Impact: The income tax generates roughly $2.6 billion annually, about one-third of Mississippi's $7 billion general fund. Its elimination would provide significant relief to Mississippi taxpayers.
2. State Grocery Sales Tax Reduction:
* Reduction: The state sales tax on groceries, currently the highest in the nation at 7%, will be reduced to 5% effective July 1, 2025.
* Impact: This reduction aims to lower living costs for all Mississippians, particularly benefiting low- and middle-income households who allocate a larger share of their income to groceries.

Tax Increases in the Build Up Mississippi Act
1. Gasoline Tax Increase:
* Increase: The state gasoline tax will rise from 18.4 cents per gallon to 27 cents per gallon by July 2027, implemented incrementally over two years.
* Purpose: The additional revenue will fund infrastructure improvements, such as roads and bridges, to support economic growth.
* Impact: This increase may disproportionately affect lower-income residents and rural drivers, though it is intended to be offset by income and grocery tax reductions.

Local Government Authority to Increase Grocery Tax
* Provision: The Build Up Mississippi Act grants local governments (municipalities and counties) the authority to impose or increase local sales taxes on groceries, provided they meet specific requirements. This provision allows local governments to offset potential revenue losses from state-level tax cuts or to fund local priorities such as schools, public safety, or infrastructure.
* Conditions: Local governments must hold a public referendum to gain voter approval for any new or increased grocery tax. The tax rate and specific use of the revenue must be clearly defined in the referendum. Additionally, any local grocery tax increase cannot result in a combined state and local grocery tax rate exceeding 7% (the current state rate before the reduction).
* Impact: Proponents claim this "flexibility" enables local governments to tailor tax policy to their communities' needs, particularly in areas where state funding for services may be strained due to the income tax phase-out. However, critics argue that local grocery tax increases could negate the benefits of the state's 5% grocery tax reduction, especially for low-income households, as groceries remain a significant expense. The regressive nature of sales taxes means that poorer residents, who spend a higher percentage of their income on essentials, could face a disproportionate burden if local taxes are raised.

Additional Notes
* Fiscal Safeguards: The Act's trigger mechanism ensures that income tax cuts beyond 2030 occur only if state revenue growth exceeds projections, protecting politicians who refuse to make significant budget cuts.
* Typo Controversy: A drafting error in the trigger formula inadvertently accelerated the income tax phase-out, prompting plans for corrective legislation in the next session.
* Economic Context: Mississippi's $700 million surplus in 2024 supports the feasibility of the tax cuts.

The Build Up Mississippi Act is a bold step toward economic transformation. However, its success will depend on politicians having the discipline to reduce wasteful spending and a continued commitment to creating positive economic incentives for businesses to grow.

# THIS is the headline Greg Abbott desperately wanted and needed. He thinks it will save his political career.
---
We believe the voters have had enough of his career politician games and will choose a new candidate in the primary. For 10 years, Abbott has jerked around the public. It is so bad, he will NOT take the stage at the state Republican convention for fear of being booed off it as John Cornyn was in 2022 for nearly 15 minutes. People are sick and tired of bullshit. We want property tax ENDED.
And these guys waste everyone's time with political theater to ban an entire industry? The people aren't falling for this crap any more. Abbott put us through enough already with his covid era love affair with lock downs, masks and mandatory nose swabs. He was on TV promoting the jabs until people started dropping dead a record numbers. Texas can and will do better than this. We don't want our lives, our health and our industries toyed around in a silly game of political theater. **So, SB3, the prohibition of all things Cannabis was vetoed a week ago in the last minutes of the veto period with less than an hour left on the clock.**
## But, quietly, SB2024 was signed into law earlier outlawing the very popular vapes and e-cigs and strictly controlling the marketing of these products which were clearly targeting kids. it goes into effect September 1, 2025.
read the version of the bill that passed and the Governor signed here:
https://legiscan.com/TX/text/SB2024/id/3220238
# Governor Abbott called a special session to start July 21st, 2205
Like most Texans, we want this legislature to go home and stay home. We don't want to give them another bite at the apple, as it were. Read more about it in the Texas Scorecard:
---
| [ ](https://email.cloud.secureclick.net/c/33448?id=2308608.862.1.054a93f7f1f30d4b90101ca8f4c6607b) Abbott calls special session, but, for what? To shake down more lobbyists and target other industries?
---
The Texas Scorecard, largely funded by Texas billionaire and conservative oilman Tim Dunn of Dallas, has a lot to say about Abbott's and Patrick's antics. You might want to subscribe and stay abreast of the many issues our state faces.
# We elected our House and Senate reps and sent them to Austin to do these important items:
**-END Property Tax** **-REFUND the over collected $33 Billion to Texas Homeowners** **-END Tax Payer Funded Lobbying** **-END Corporate Welfare** **-SHRINK Government** **-FINISH the Texas Border Wall (800 miles still unprotected with Mexico)** **-END ALL DEI EVERYWHERE** **-BAN mRNA in anything in Texas** **-Take the porn out of schools** _Have you ever had a dog that once it snuck out of the front door acted like you didn't exist?_ _You call their name and they refuse to even look your way or acknowledge you, even resisting when you run them down grab them by the collar..._ Legislators I've known for years were doing just that this session. Literally running away and hiding. They had been given their orders by Dick Weekly's TLR and they followed the playbook. Yes...there is an actual 3 ring binder from TLR and many of them walk around the House floor with it on their desk or in their hands. Dick Weekly and his group dumped $12 Million into what your thought were YOUR legislators. That is just the 2024 donation figure. Yes, Dick purchased your legislators right out from under you. Oh, now, I know they'll protest and tell you they have to take the money because "its hard being in Austin" and "I still vote the way I vote" kind of answers. Well, we watched you guys pass some stupid legislation glorifying the Islamic take over of some communities and more this session. So, those cover stories just don't make any sense.
# We stil have:
**-Skyrocketing Property Tax** **-Tax Payer Funded Lobbying** **-they expanded Corporate Welfare** **-they spent our $33 Billion** **-they expanded the budget by 44%** **-Texas Govt grew to its largest in history this session** **-The House killed the border wall bill...we have no backup** **-Refused to ban mRNA** **-DEI by its many names still funded by your tax dollars** **-PORN still in your kids schools** And Abbott just called a special session so these same people can go do some more damage? For God's sake, send them home and tell them to quit messing with our state.
---
**Kind regards,** **JL Trahan** **BIZPAC Founder and Executive Chairman**

Day Three of the 2021 Hunger Strike with Zohran and NYTWA
| | | Pinch me! Last Tuesday Zohran Mamdani beat Andrew Cuomo decisively in the Democratic primary for Mayor of NYC and I am still in profound and happy shock. It seemed impossible that anyone would beat Cuomo three months ago, and extremely unlikely that Mamdani, outspoken critic of Israel's atrocities in Gaza and advocate for free buses and freezing rent, could overcome millions of Michael Bloomberg's money being spent against him. Elite media wants to put it down to charisma and viral videos, but clearly, what Zohran was saying and what he stands for struck a deep chord. One fact I think hasn't gone nearly enough attention: he had 50,000 volunteers. That means almost _one in twenty five_ voters were also volunteers. I've never seen anything like it. The tired chant, "this is what democracy looks like" often just means "this is what protest looks like," not self-government. The campaign gives me hope because those 50,000 people live in the city, work in the city, the volunteer operation is not a separate fact of people's lives, but an integrated one. A machine like that, without promise of a job, means that tens of thousands of mostly young people saw or heard something about Mamdani's politics that made them give up TikTok and the Mets, and sign up to walk through apartment buildings and meet strangers and talk to them.They knocked on more doors than there were primary votes. (1.5 to 1.1 million). Another way to put it is that its very exciting that the big rejoinder to Trump is coming from a _municipal_ election, where it is possible to imagine politics and discussion and real debate happening at scale. Get involved locally. Here's the election night speech, well worth the watch, about how affordability and democracy need not be two separate dreams:
> [_A New Dawn for New York City_](https://the-antimonopolist.ghost.io/r/338a2d93?m=46b412a0-1cbe-4fcb-b85d-2477ce9f4e21)
At the Mamdani election night party the first person I saw was Bhairavi Desai, the leader of the [New York Taxi Workers Alliance](https://the-antimonopolist.ghost.io/r/a69a9f87?m=46b412a0-1cbe-4fcb-b85d-2477ce9f4e21), an incredible group of Taxi, Uber and Lyft drivers (I profiled them in my last book, [Break 'em Up](https://the-antimonopolist.ghost.io/r/f3c20e8f?m=46b412a0-1cbe-4fcb-b85d-2477ce9f4e21)). NYC Taxi drivers were dying by suicide, crushed by debt and abandoned by the very systems that were supposed to protect them. In response, NYTWA and dozens of taxi drivers, mostly immigrants and many elderly, launched a hunger strike. For 45 days, they protested the crushing medallion debt that their fellow taxi drivers faced. Newly elected [Assemblymember Zohran Mamdani, along with Assemblymember Yuh-Line Niou,](https://the-antimonopolist.ghost.io/r/35deafc4?m=46b412a0-1cbe-4fcb-b85d-2477ce9f4e21) moved to the protest site. They fasted for 15 days alongside the drivers, until they eventually won--also very much against the odds. Speaking of local politics--on the other side of the country--it was through the fight led by the New York Taxi Workers Alliance that I met another politician you should pay attention to and support, [David Seligman](https://the-antimonopolist.ghost.io/r/17cd1567?m=46b412a0-1cbe-4fcb-b85d-2477ce9f4e21). Seligman pointed out that Uber and Lyft looked like they were engaging in wage fixing in NYC. He has also sued Uber, and helped drivers organize, and was one of the few lawyers in the country who understood how corporate power weaponizes the law and how to fight back. He was relentless.[David is now running for Colorado attorney general. ](https://the-antimonopolist.ghost.io/r/0191c499?m=46b412a0-1cbe-4fcb-b85d-2477ce9f4e21)I think its a good test of a good politician where they stand vis a vis Uber. David is one of the fiercest antimonopoly lawyers in the country. He takes on exploitative bosses, abusive landlords, Silicon Valley giants, _anyone_ who profits from rigging the system against working people._Obviously,_ corporate interests are already trying to stop him. If you can, please help [give early support to David Seligman](https://the-antimonopolist.ghost.io/r/4c9fbacb?m=46b412a0-1cbe-4fcb-b85d-2477ce9f4e21) in his Attorney General's race? It would be really amazing to have him in that role as we build this antimonopoly movement nationally. Thanks. In solidarity,Zephyr TeachoutPS: I did a shift of volunteering in a set of upper west side rent stabilized buildings, and, right between where Cuomo won and Mamdani won, the doors were not easy, but that's what made them meaningful. One woman (who we convinced! told us how comforting Cuomo had been during Covid. Another (who we did not) shouted at us all the way down the hall. These were real conversations, some of them lasting 15 or twenty minutes. The young women I canvassed with were in their twenties, and we had a lot fun, but it was far more engaged and curious than most door-knocking I've done; we learned things, the people at the doors learned things, and we talked about politics in an open honest way-this wasn't some microtargeting effort to exploit individual biases. Maybe we can rebuild democracy after all. Support this newsletter [here.](https://the-antimonopolist.ghost.io/r/bfc3756e?m=46b412a0-1cbe-4fcb-b85d-2477ce9f4e21)

body:
They're playbook is tired, but we're not.
# [](https://act.ilhanomar.com/go/35?t=1&akid=1692%2E791427%2ETGy4z-)

Friend,
I want to be real with you for a minute. Ilhan and I, our families, and our staff face personal risks every day doing this work.
And sometimes people say to me, “Well, that’s what you signed up for.”
Last month, the White House came after me for calling out their BS. Last week, MAGA Twitter personalities attacked me with degrading slurs. Next week, it’ll be someone else. There’s something about taking up space in the halls of power as an unapologetic, bald Black woman that really gets under their skin – but I digress.
**Their tired playbook is the same as it’s always been. Racist dogwhistles and thinly veiled threats.**
And every time this happens, my staff and I face an increase in physical threats.
To be clear, no person in any profession – and certainly no public servant – signed up for the vitriol, abuse, harassment, physical threats, and violence that come with this job. No one deserves that. Any rhetoric that creates a permission structure for people to resolve political differences with violence should be vigorously condemned.
**[If you’re able, you can show your support by making a donation right now. Your contribution will fuel our fight and ensure we can keep speaking truth to power.**](https://act.ilhanomar.com/go/7?c0=ap-em-june2025-io.0EmSpx&refcode=em250630-1-90&t=2&akid=1692%2E791427%2ETGy4z-)

Y’all know me – I’ll continue to speak up and fight back with every tool available. But I do want to say this:
My team, my colleagues, and I make innumerable personal sacrifices for this movement. We spend more time with each other than we do own families, all because we care about this work. All because we believe in the power and the possibility of a better world and the transformative impact that government can have in our lives.
Every empty attack on me is an attack on all of us. On our families. On our ability to show up and be accessible to constituents in the world every day.
I'm not afraid, I'm not deterred, I won't be silenced. I know that the vile acts of political violence – the attacks on Minnesota lawmakers, the dehumanizing bodyslam of Senator Padilla, the lawless arrest of Congresswoman MacGyver – were simply because they were doing the jobs they were elected to do.
None of this is happening in a vacuum. This is all coordinated. It is meant to silence us. It is meant to discourage, to dissuade, and to marginalize.
Well, we're not backing down. We will continue to do the work that people deserve for us to do on their behalf.

clean_body: | | | | | | | | Dear Fellow Conservative, Do you support President Trump’s work to slash our bloated federal government? Are you a fan of the nearly $160 BILLION+ in spending cuts that the Department of Government Efficiency (or DOGE) have made so far? Do you love when President Trump talks about dismantling the Department of Education or firing thousands of overpaid, unaccountable Deep State bureaucrats? Because this is the moment you and I have been waiting for! For decades, conservative seniors like you and me have been hoping and praying for a president who would actually shrink our federal government. And with President Trump in office, we finally have a historic opportunity to undo decades of reckless, unchecked growth. We cannot let this slip through our fingers! Because liberal groups like the AARP will be trying to undermine President Trump and DOGE every step of the way. I believe the AARP has betrayed seniors like you and me. They’re claiming they speak for us -- and they’re using seniors as an excuse to push an extreme far-left agenda that goes against everything you and I stand for. With your survey, you’re telling President Trump that the AARP DOES NOT speak for you -- or ANY conservative senior... With your survey, you’re making sure they know conservative seniors fully support DOGE’s work to slash wasteful spending, fire useless bureaucrats, abolish pointless government agencies, and root out millions of dollars of fraud and abuse... And with your survey, you’re proudly declaring this is exactly what you voted for. Your swift action is critical. The AARP already threw Seniors like you and me “under the bus” during President Trump’s first administration by blocking his attempts to repeal Obamacare and give you more control of your health care. If you and I don’t make our voices heard right now, it will be too late. Liberal groups like the AARP will successfully undermine DOGE’s efforts, and this once-in-a-lifetime opportunity will pass us by. My name is Rebecca Weber. I’m a fellow Senior, and I’m the head of AMAC Action. If you’ve heard of us, you know that “AMAC” stands for the Association of Mature American Citizens. And “Action” is what we’re known for. When it comes to standing up for the rights of Conservative Seniors like you... ...no other advocacy group in the nation is more influential than AMAC Action. AMAC Action is a force to be reckoned with in Washington. With 75 chapters, 300 delegates, and now more than 2 MILLION AMAC members and rapidly growing -- we’re fighting for YOU. Our “feet on the street” advocates contact Members of Congress and state legislators on your behalf. And 400,000 AMAC advocates (and counting!) have sent over a million messages to Congress, state legislatures, and regulatory agencies like the FTC, HHS, and CMS to make sure the voice of Conservative Seniors is heard on key issues. During President Trump’s first term in office, we were a treasured resource. → President Trump called us to the White House to tell him what AMAC members thought about historic regulatory reform. → We were right there in the Rose Garden when President Trump announced a life- saving AMAC-supported plan that reduces insulin costs for you and your loved ones. → Two of our AMAC members were invited to the White House to meet with the President, Vice President, Attorney General, police officers, and other select citizens to discuss the best ways to protect our brave police. → And when AMAC Action bombarded the Governors of New York, New Jersey, Pennsylvania, and Michigan -- questioning their fatal decision to send COVID-19 contagious patients from hospitals to nursing homes resulting in the deaths of thousands of Seniors -- President Trump’s Department of Justice took action. Now that he’s back in the White House, AMAC Action is fighting alongside President Trump for YOU and for your fellow Conservative Seniors across the country once again. While the AARP spent last year showing noncitizens how to access Medicare, and propping up the disaster that is Obamacare... ...AMAC Action has been busy fighting for YOU -- and that will continue through 2025 and beyond. We’re not about to let the Liberal AARP pretend like they speak for America’s Seniors -- and we’re not about to let this historic moment slip through our fingers. And today I’m hoping you’ll join us. And if you’re ready to seize this historic opportunity and finally shrink our oversized federal government... ...would you make a one-time gift of $35 when you submit your survey? My friend, your gift of $35 to AMAC Action will help send and collect more SENIORS’ DOGE SURVEYS from conservative seniors just like you -- seniors who won’t let this once-in-a-lifetime chance pass us by... ...and who won’t sit back quietly and let liberal groups like the AARP undermine President Trump and DOGE. And if you’re able to give even more today -- say $50, $75, $125, $250, $500, or even $1,000, your gift will make an even greater impact. Because when you give to AMAC Action... → Your gift RALLIES our grassroots network of 2 million AMAC members when lawmakers threaten your freedom or your hard-earned benefits. → Your gift POWERS our efforts to support DOGE -- and all of President Trump’s work to make America great again. → And your gift HOLDS lawmakers’ feet to the fire and ensures they work with President Trump to shrink our government, cut wasteful spending, root out the Deep State, and usher in the next great Golden Age of America. | | Hi Friend,
---
I hope you’re having a good start to your summer.
---

---
But it’s a big week for another, not so great, reason. If Trump and Republicans in Congress have their way, I’ll be heading back to Washington, D.C. to vote on their big, bad bill for billionaires. And I’m a big NO.
---
I’ve been working hard against this bill from the start. Cutting Medicaid, SNAP, Pell Grants, and energy programs will make many in our country sicker, hungrier, less educated, and poorer. Congressional Republicans are gutting these programs and growing our national debt by trillions so that the wealthiest Americans get a tax giveaway they don’t need. It’s not fair.
---
A recent poll said Americans want our government to help lower costs for health care, utilities, and food. This big ugly bill Trump and Republicans are racing to pass raises all of those costs. It’s a reverse Robin Hood scheme: it takes from the poor to give to the rich, hurting everyone along the way.
---
I’ll be honest: today is a big deadline for our team — the last day of this fundraising reporting period. When the reports for the last three months come out, people will ask if I’m on track to have a strong campaign and help lead the effort to win back the House of Representatives.

#

GOOD MORNING!
It’s June 30th. We’re right at the midpoint of the year. Mark’s staring down an important fundraising deadline at midnight — an official FEC deadline — and we’re hoping you might be able to make a donation before then.
If you can, use this link:

Mark couldn’t stay on the sidelines anymore. If he could make a difference by helping take back control of the United States Senate, he was going to do it.

With Trump in the White House for his second term, Mark’s taken the lead in facing him down and picking righteous fights — to defend our democracy and do what’s right for Arizona and the entire country.

Normally when you see my name in your inbox, I like the messages to be different from the other emails you get from most elected officials.
#

Peter,
Normally when you see my name in your inbox, I like the messages to be different from the other emails you get from most elected officials.
I've written to you in detail about the depth of corruption and self-enrichment of the Trump Administration, the President's thirst for political retribution and intimidation, along with other things I am seeing or working on in Washington, D.C. and at home in Georgia.
This message is different. It's more direct.
I am reaching out this morning with a last-ditch request for a contribution to my campaign before our June FEC fundraising drive comes to a close at midnight. Here's why:
This race will be one of the most competitive and expensive in the nation. I am the only Democratic Senator up for re-election in a state Trump won in 2024 and that makes me MAGA’s #1 target.
In 2020, the pundits said flipping a Republican Senate seat in Georgia couldn’t be done. But we built one of the strongest voter mobilization programs in Senate campaign history – and we won. That victory won the Senate majority.
Now we must win again. And we will win again.
Just like last time, I can’t do it alone.

**Let me be clear: I love President Trump and I’ve been behind him 100% every day for the last 10 years.**
But what we’re seeing right now is not President Trump’s agenda, it’s the neocons and RINOs taking advantage of the broken system in Washington.
Just last week the far-left Senate Parliamentarian stripped some of the most important language from the Big Beautiful Bill which means it will continue funding sex changes on kids, Medicare and Medicaid for illegal immigrants, and strips the ability of states to regulate the use of AI for 10 years.
Six months ago I was so excited and felt like we could do anything with full Republican control of the government, _now it feels like there is nothing we can do._

subject: Let’s Keep Going

body:
ELIZABETH PANNILL FLETCHER FOR CONGRESS [https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/NGP/NGP10/1/82676/images/Non-Re-Elect%20Logo.png]
It’s been a tough month. And a tough year. And that is why I am so incredibly grateful to everyone on #TeamLizzie for the wonderful support you have given me and the team. It keeps me, and all of us, going.
And keep going, we must. As you have seen by now, the threats of redrawing Texas’ congressional maps are increasing, as Washington Republicans see it as a tool to use to try and keep the House majority. We don’t know what’s going to happen yet—or what reaction it will cause. But we do know we need to be ready.
We were born ready. This team has been working together against the odds and for the people since 2017. And we aren’t stopping now.
Today is the last day of the reporting period before for the Federal Election Commission. As we navigate the next few months, the financial report we submit will be the one people will see when assessing the strength of our team. You can make a contribution [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/lpfe250630?refcode=lpfe250630] here to help us end this quarter in the best possible financial position.
The stakes are getting higher every day—for what we stand to lose, but also for what we stand to gain. In 2026, we have the opportunity to win back the House majority so we can protect our rights, advance equality, and strengthen our democracy.
We know what it takes to fight and to win because we have done it before. In 2018 we made history together when we flipped this seat from red to blue—and in the years since, we have built a winning coalition here on Team Lizzie.
Now, as the Republican Congress works to pass a budget that will harm people from sea to shining sea, our work together has never been more important.
If you’re in a position to make a contribution before the FEC fundraising deadline tonight, your support will help us not just to hold this seat, but to help take back the House in 2026. [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/lpfe250630?refcode=lpfe250630]
Together, we can do anything,

body:
| Peter, I want you to know something: From the start, this campaign has been about you — not political insiders or mega corporations, and never about power or personal gain. At the heart of this campaign are people you know: a union worker, a single mom, a grocery clerk, and a neighbor who’s had enough. We’re caring, everyday folks who want a representative who shows up and delivers for North Carolina families. While billionaires and special interest groups get ready to back our new opponent hand-picked by Donald Trump, we’re building something I’m really proud of: a grassroots campaign fueled by supporters like you. We don't rely on scare tactics, fake deadlines, or pressure you with gimmicks. Peter,

I’m Adam Schwarze—former Navy SEAL Officer, Marine Corps veteran, and proud Minnesotan.

I’ve deployed nine times to 70 countries to serve this great country. I never expected to run for the U.S. Senate. But when I returned home and saw what was happening to Minnesota—when I saw the radical left rising—I knew I had to step up.

_**And now I need your help.**_

The same Democratic Socialist movement that just **[hijacked New York City is gaining ground here in the Midwest.](http://links.bestamericanow.com/u/click?_t=f6e78b69acbb4291bd75bc93fae35a62&_m=a99a50e1f14443dd9b2e954fd5579f6e&_e=v-qdcN5fd0nubLW8IUGPWI9jFpJbJ4hMohW27WKYjqY4hpVEdD6A7db5srQ5918OK6L22qN5hlF1JKE4EJ9792aAVPNd8_WpdbEbuYEfgw79lZW7hAsQrcCugSZciSWl0_lQJFj6CIl6lW4UkZUy1NWabLc4F-8N7rx6Li4OP7WnnRNpuIevhxLO7a3v3tug2zZ0HGiO7X9rCqcBGc1oDnjIGb2e2oY_JBEdr8qzAalBLgZudE9j2MAJLHjkG6pSVMeM3WzhQdfUNtiRGEpUcNY373Wvz7fFnXdTLJOnl2ziBiaVTjL2OqxlMfsFX2nehiXsjHhDUQJGdHkv_ygbjW6H5DrKiwspjFT_-EY9T8CbfybdSjUW6rub4pQ6mtUysD_by6-zXlUwvEWMQ62sjXKcSof940e1OEbjdmYxAcmXI2LAjZ941knJQLHep-UZyJEon0itOSCIHcJSDkg54WaI4ob0ItTRgWdj9j2TQ6DUbq5gdqWM-JG6c6PsjvZjdYz60aqhLbRyk3siqDRWgeBhpas5ACK1fCAJZ5rgtNVqhKRs6rTmjS4VGYeK0LFKcRxGgmoQZ3QlUFiz26g_fEYABgl_6fXLBsqU5zx6ZSqq9GFiZl6x67mKW9EE-SwFwGvfcdGN_fovslZsNYSb8dVkYoRT3ym8DdDpnbgPDx78xEpEkZtvQFZVKk6ukahQCzrhYAyG-6WQhBZFw7af6ivYiSmeUIuJA2nYIlPFiU-X6EIP7x0tVEMa-40f5Zti) **This week, New York Democrats nominated a man so extreme that he promised to arrest the Israeli Prime Minister and replace city police with social workers. If that sounds insane, it is.

_**But don’t think it’s limited to the coasts.**_****

My opponent—the lieutenant governor of Minnesota—isn’t far behind. She openly aligned with violent unrest in 2020, **pushed to dismantle our police, and filed lawsuits against law enforcement as our communities burned. While Governor Walz tried to save face, she doubled down on chaos.**

This kind of radicalism isn’t an outlier anymore. It’s the new blueprint of the left. And if we don’t draw the line in Minnesota, it will keep spreading.

The Minnesota I grew up in—where you respected your neighbors, honored your country, and stood for law and order—feels like it’s slipping away.

**I didn’t wait to serve my country after 9/11. I enlisted on my 18th birthday and spent over 20 years protecting American freedom abroad. Now I’m fighting to protect it at home. **

I don’t come from money or a political legacy. I come from grit, faith, and a calling to serve. That’s what drives me now.

_**It may be too late for New York, but there is still hope for the rest of us.

[**HELP ME STOP SOCIALISM IN MINNESOTA**](http://links.bestamericanow.com/u/click?_t=f6e78b69acbb4291bd75bc93fae35a62&_m=a99a50e1f14443dd9b2e954fd5579f6e&_e=v-qdcN5fd0nubLW8IUGPWI9jFpJbJ4hMohW27WKYjqY4hpVEdD6A7db5srQ5918OK6L22qN5hlF1JKE4EJ9792aAVPNd8_WpdbEbuYEfgw79lZW7hAsQrcCugSZciSWl0_lQJFj6CIl6lW4UkZUy1NWabLc4F-8N7rx6Li4OP7WnnRNpuIevhxLO7a3v3tug2zZ0HGiO7X9rCqcBGc1oDnjIGb2e2oY_JBEdr8qzAalBLgZudE9j2MAJLHjkG6pSVMeM3WzhQdfUNtiRGEpUcO3BjYiKCu30cLABAA3Wnglf30HxIhp9cY9KXfgcgskJLG3_Xxhe7whbDb2yRbyuqf5gqL7YVk43ai7qTtKdh06WAEYi0KJWZF2EGGqpjdZkbtfdUfVBHsjvMSs2ooNazwj307CFSMQOk71MK9KQDG10XPcIVSi8ERxS0l1uUkyUpvSZ1CvKBeTM9tqMgqjYtydJjuAbI_gx6tmqoRBSRiylCGUKMWydHAl6ecRgVxAP-XjN-DdCV6PWt5QnTLEgnDUmImAfHjvcev_OtQ9d1EBxlr5GrPdJn9t7v4Rz225NPTMWrqu8jffqWF7l1tm2qhM8kL7cGT2nRroiBhhv4sVGNIRGstxLqxHE0WKaXfQlfLX7OH709cWdg8eTcN6WuM_HmcK7kAQgJid9bcP2kFhbCK8vsVXX1dLarJ-3MMU-1VyIim9wPR7qH2KjWg2KEf_BcjGaAFtHowZNe9tpHtzSVPQeT0lroNiuLZNX0xRw) **_

This election isn’t just about one Senate seat. It’s about stopping a national wave of socialist extremism that threatens to bankrupt small businesses, rewrite our values, and destroy what millions of Americans fought and died to defend.

New York may have fallen to it. **But Minnesota doesn’t have to.**

If you’ve ever felt like your voice doesn’t matter anymore, it does. The radical left is organized, loud, and well-funded. But they don’t speak for most of us.

**We need a new kind of leadership—rooted in service, not self-interest.**

clean_body: It may be too late for New York, but there is still hope for the rest of us. | Peter, I’m Adam Schwarze—former Navy SEAL Officer, Marine Corps veteran, and proud Minnesotan. I’ve deployed nine times to 70 countries to serve this great country. I never expected to run for the U.S. Senate. But when I returned home and saw what was happening to Minnesota—when I saw the radical left rising—I knew I had to step up. And now I need your help. The same Democratic Socialist movement that just This week, New York Democrats nominated a man so extreme that he promised to arrest the Israeli Prime Minister and replace city police with social workers. If that sounds insane, it is. But don’t think it’s limited to the coasts.** My opponent—the lieutenant governor of Minnesota—isn’t far behind. She openly aligned with violent unrest in 2020, pushed to dismantle our police, and filed lawsuits against law enforcement as our communities burned. While Governor Walz tried to save face, she doubled down on chaos. This kind of radicalism isn’t an outlier anymore. It’s the new blueprint of the left. And if we don’t draw the line in Minnesota, it will keep spreading. The Minnesota I grew up in—where you respected your neighbors, honored your country, and stood for law and order—feels like it’s slipping away. I didn’t wait to serve my country after 9/11. I enlisted on my 18th birthday and spent over 20 years protecting American freedom abroad. Now I’m fighting to protect it at home. I don’t come from money or a political legacy. I come from grit, faith, and a calling to serve. That’s what drives me now. It may be too late for New York, but there is still hope for the rest of us. This election isn’t just about one Senate seat. It’s about stopping a national wave of socialist extremism that threatens to bankrupt small businesses, rewrite our values, and destroy what millions of Americans fought and died to defend. New York may have fallen to it. But Minnesota doesn’t have to. If you’ve ever felt like your voice doesn’t matter anymore, it does. The radical left is organized, loud, and well-funded. But they don’t speak for most of us. We need a new kind of leadership—rooted in service, not self-interest. If you’re not ready to donate today, that’s okay. clean_body: | | | | | Dear Peter, It’s hard to believe 2025 is already halfway over! God has moved powerfully over the past six months, and we’re full of faith for what He’ll do in the months ahead. But to keep this ministry going strong through the rest of 2025 and beyond, we need your help. At Let Us Worship, our heart is to bring worship as a free gift—no admission required. Just show up as you are and encounter the presence of God. We’ve heard countless testimonies of people drawn in by the sound of worship, encountering the Holy Spirit and having their lives transformed. We’re able to offer these revivals for free because of supporters like you—an army of Believers pouring out prayer, time, and resources. Let Us Worship is entirely donor-funded. But to keep it that way, we need your support before our fundraising deadline ends TONIGHT at midnight! Putting on a revival takes a massive effort—musicians, production, support staff, permits, and logistics—all without charging a cover fee. That’s why we’re asking: will you chip in today to keep these revivals free for all? We don’t ask often—just at the end of each quarter or when major needs arise. And tonight at midnight, the quarter ends. Will you stand with us and help fund what’s next? Your gift fuels the mission of Let Us Worship and helps us prepare for what’s ahead. Fellow activist,

Today marks the deadline for the Pennsylvania budget process. As a reminder, our state budget is a moral document – where state legislators have a unique opportunity to pass legislation to counteract the Trump regime’s “Big Beautiful Bill” and instead move critical issues forward, such as raising our minimum wage, fairly funding K-12 and higher education, legalizing adult-use marijuana, and defending abortion access.

But here’s the thing: PA’s funding priorities are going to be set well before Trump’s bill gets signed into law, which means we may have major gaps in our budget. As Governor Shapiro stated in the _Pennsylvania Capital-Star_ , “Any lawmaker in D.C. who thinks the commonwealth can backfill this massive hole they’ve created is wrong – and these cuts will have real life consequences for Pennsylvanians.”
**Who we elect, from Washington to our state legislature, the courts, and beyond, has major implications for our state.** That is why it’s so critical that we engage our centered communities on the ground and make sure voters understand the role that elected officials play in their everyday lives.
**However, as the second quarter comes to a close, we are noticing that funding is not moving as quickly as we had anticipated. That means grassroots individual donations are more important than ever. **

**In order to maintain our current level of operations and to ramp up as we prepare for the crucial Supreme Court retention elections and other judicial, local and municipal elections happening in Pennsylvania this year, we need your help. **

[**As a reminder, all donations up to $50,000 will be MATCHED – we need your help to hit that goal and take full advantage of this opportunity.

We need your help to reach voters across the Commonwealth to ensure they understand what’s at stake and are prepared to turn out to hold legislators accountable who prioritize billionaires over the hardworking people of our state. Help fund our voter engagement and civic education programs so we can achieve a more representative democracy that works for everyone, not just a select few, by rushing $25 or more before MIDNIGHT.
